newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 17.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Motorola Inc plans a $12.9 billion satellite network designed to deliver high-speed data and video to businesses, broadcasters and telecommunications companies.
* Genesis Health Ventures Inc and two investment companies have agreed to acquire Multicare Cos Inc for $1.05 billion plus $342 million in assumed debt.
* Oppenheimer & Co is planning to stop processing trades for a brokerage-firm client accused of charging excessive commissions.

* Trans-Atlantic airline alliances hae driven up prices and limited competition on some routes, an issue that may come into play as regulators review the deal between AMR Corp's American Airlines and British Airways Plc.
* G-7 leaders are set to release policies this week aimed at heading off or containing potential crises that arise from the globalization of financial markets.
* France and Germany reached a compromise on the goals of growth and fiscal discipline, allowing plans for a common European currency to remain on track.

* B.A.T Industries Plc Chief Executive Martin Broughton has helped persuade Philip Morris Cos Inc and RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp not to back off from their stance onthe punitive-damages issue in the tobacco settlement talks.
* General Motors Corp and the United Auto Workers union reported progress for the first time in weeks in talks aimed at ending a strike at a Pontiac, Mich., truck plant.
* Eastman Kodak Co ended its longtime relationship with advertising agency J. Walter Thompson, signing up Ogilvy & Mather to conduct its consumer-imaging products ad campaign.
* The U.S. Supreme Court dismissed a whistleblower lawsuit against a unit of General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp .
* Amgen Inc expects a "modest reduction" in the 1997 growth rate of its Epogen drug as a result of changes in Medicare's reimbursement policy.
* Louis Navellier has won a vote a confidence from shareholders of a fund from which he was ousted earlier this year.
* The California Public Employees' Retirement System unveiled a set of proposed governance guidelines for U.S. companies in its $113 billion portfolio.
* Heard on the Street: The Russell small-cap indexes are about to undergo their annual revision, and they are likely to emerge with a younger and more technology-oriented group of stocks.
* Credit Markets: Bond prices rose a day ahead of the government's report on the consumer price index, one of the most closely watched U.S. inflation indicators.
